canonicalTypes.Government & Civic: Town halls, courts, permits, registry offices, guard headquarters, ministries, civic bureaus, customs, command offices.
canonicalTypes.Religious & Spiritual: Temples, shrines, cathedrals, monasteries, funerary sites, memorial necropolises, worship offices, divine containment liaison sites.
canonicalTypes.Medical, Alchemy & Ichor: Apothecaries, clinics, hospitals, potion exchanges, alchemy stores, ichor-regulated medical offices, sanitariums.
canonicalTypes.Commercial & Retail: Markets, general stores, provisioning, furniture, jewelry, exchanges, bazaars, supply counters, pawnshops, merchant streets.
canonicalTypes.Food, Drink & Hospitality: Taverns, inns, hostels, hotels, bakeries, butcher shops, restaurants, tea houses, bathhouses, common houses.
canonicalTypes.Education, Archives & Lore: Schools, universities, libraries, archives, museums, scroll offices, research districts, cartographers, newspapers.
canonicalTypes.Industry & Crafting: Blacksmiths, foundries, workshops, mills, ropeworks, clockwork halls, engine works, shipwrights, forges, repair yards.
canonicalTypes.Agriculture, Animals & Food Supply: Farms, stables, orchards, greenhouses, kennels, hunting lodges, fisheries, kelp farms, familiar breeders, granaries.
canonicalTypes.Nature & Wilderness: Parks, gardens, groves, ranger sites, wilderness preserves, forest pools, sanctuaries, moss gardens.
canonicalTypes.Maritime & Waterfront: Harbors, docks, piers, wharves, fishing sites, lighthouses, sailmakers, reef sites, coastal and water-facing places.
canonicalTypes.Residential & Social Care: Houses, apartments, boarding houses, orphanages, poorhouses, refugee quarters, worker housing, tenements.
canonicalTypes.Noble, Elite & Prestige: Palaces, noble estates, royal quarters, luxury districts, grand hotels, prestige institutions.
canonicalTypes.Criminal, Vice & Underground: Black markets, smugglers, pirate sites, lawless alleys, undercities, gambling dens, hidden rebel platforms.
canonicalTypes.Transportation & Logistics: Rail, caravan, ferry, steamship, skyship, submarine, portals, freight, warehouses, stations, terminals, route offices.
canonicalTypes.Special, Hazards & Adventure Sites: Ruins, divine prison rumor-sites, storm shelters, disaster shelters, haunted pools, ancient hazards, unique hooks.
canonicalTypes.Other / Flexible: Locations that can be assigned by DM or by additional rules based on settlement context.

Capital City.Most Likely Transit Modes: Rail, caravan, ferry/steamship, skyship, portal if capital

City.Most Likely Transit Modes: Rail, caravan, ferry/steamship, skyship if large

Town.Most Likely Transit Modes: Caravan, rail platform, ferry if water-linked

Village.Most Likely Transit Modes: Caravan, ferry, foot/animal routes; rail only if strategically placed

Settlement-bound residents.frequency: Rarely leave settlement; may visit nearby outskirts monthly or seasonally.
Settlement-bound residents.bestUses: Most homes, local shops, civic labor, elderly households, dependent households.

Local district / daily commuters.frequency: Daily or weekly movement inside the settlement, district, harbor, rail stop, worksite, mine, farm, or shrine area.
Local district / daily commuters.bestUses: Workers, students, guards, service staff, market workers, healers, apprentices.

Same-province routine travelers.frequency: Weekly, monthly, or seasonal movement between settlements in one province.
Same-province routine travelers.bestUses: Merchants, guild workers, clergy, couriers, artisans, caravan crews, fishers, harvest workers.

Inter-province travelers.frequency: Monthly to quarterly, or whenever duty demands.
Inter-province travelers.bestUses: Faction agents, trade officers, diplomats, skyship crews, rail command, major clergy, nobles, expedition workers.

Seasonal / itinerant travelers.frequency: Arrive for routes, harvests, storms, trade seasons, festivals, pilgrimages, repairs, and crisis work.
Seasonal / itinerant travelers.bestUses: Performers, migrant labor, pilgrims, salvage crews, caravan workers, monster hunters, mercenary labor.

Elite, faction, or restricted-route trav.frequency: Irregular but high-impact; movement creates records, rumors, and faction consequences.
Elite, faction, or restricted-route trav.bestUses: Tiered faction officers, ATA-cleared travelers, ambassadors, sanctioned couriers, high merchants, divine heralds.

biomeTravelAdjustments.adjustment: +3 to +8 percentage points to same-province and inter-province travel if harbors, ferries, steamships, or reef trade are active. Increase Maritime and Transit locations.

+5 to restricted-route and specialist travel; lower casual day visitors unless submarine terminals are common. Submarine crews, pressure engineers, reef surveyors, and salvage routes create transient worker pressure.
+2 to seasonal/itinerant travel during harvest, herd movement, trade fairs, and caravan seasons. Villages stay more settlement-bound outside those periods.
+3 to regional travel if mines, rail tunnels, gear-lifts, or sky-pass routes exist. Reduce casual visitors if passes are dangerous.
+4 to restricted-route, same-province, or faction movement; lower tourist movement unless the cavern is a trade hub. Underdeep routes and sealed corridors make travel political.
+2 to local and same-province travel through ranger, grove, hunter, and herbal routes; reduce inter-province travel unless rail, skyship, or portal access exists.
+3 to local commuter movement through ropeways, lifts, canopy paths, and vertical workplaces. Reduce heavy freight unless lift stations and ground depots exist.
+3 to same-province route movement by ferry, reed boat, guide path, smuggler route, or raised rail. Increase criminal/underground travel pressure if danger is high.

implementationSteps.instruction: Choose biome profile and settlement type.
Use the biome percentage table to allocate location types. Round only at the final location count.
Pull specific location names from the matching JSON pool when available; otherwise use nearest biome and settlement-size pool.
Apply danger level, alignment phase, race cache, faction pressure, and transit requirements as modifiers after the base location percentages.
Assign NPC travel behavior by settlement type. Then adjust for biome and transit infrastructure.
Ensure every generated settlement has food supply, housing, medical access, civic order, at least one transit path appropriate to biome, and a plausible reason people stay or travel.
